newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares drift lower on fuel fare hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares drift lower on fuel fare hike fears.

text.p: Delhi shares closed lower on Thursday as traders adopted a cautious approach in view of a likely rise in prices of petroleum products, brokers said.
The bourse's sensitive index fell 1.92 points to close at 770.41.
"Despite the recovery, operators were not ready to enlarge their commitment in view of a likely hike in petroleum prices," said Yogesh Sethi of brokers Vinayaka Investments.
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral says the government plans to take a bold decision on cutting losses due to a subsidy the state pays oil firms to sell petroleum products cheaply.
India's oil pool deficit rose to 155 billion rupees ($4.33 billion) at the end of 1996/97 (April-March).

The deficit -- the money owed by the government to the oil companies for oil products below market prices -- will hit 245 billion rupees by the end of this fiscal year if nothing is done, according to junior Petroleum Minister T.R Balu.
ITC rose 11.85 rupees to 421.30 on sustained buying by foreign investors, brokers said.
State Bank of India closed 1.90 rupees lower at 303.25.
